subproblems.title: Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector is at most √(P^n) times its operator norm
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every n-covector α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n = Eucl P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ, with ‖α‖ its operator norm as a continuous alternating map: covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ √(P^n)·‖α‖. Here covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} t_I), where t_I = α(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)})² if I is strictly increasing and t_I = 0 otherwise, and b_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i is the standard basis of ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ Real.sqrt ((P : ℝ) ^ n) * ‖α‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation:
- b_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i for i : Fin P.
- For I : Fin n → Fin P, v_I := (i ↦ b_{I(i)}) : Fin n → Eucl P.
- t_I := (α v_I)² if StrictMono I, and t_I := 0 otherwise.
Unfolding the definition (unfold covectorEuclideanNorm), covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_I t_I). The sum runs over the finite type Fin n → Fin P.

1. Each b_i is a unit vector: b_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), and ‖EuclideanSpace.single i 1‖ = ‖(1 : ℝ)‖ = 1 (simp). Hence ∏_{i : Fin n} ‖b_{I(i)}‖ = 1 for every I.
2. For every I, ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm gives ‖α v_I‖ ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖b_{I(i)}‖, which equals ‖α‖ by step 1. On ℝ, ‖·‖ = |·| (Real.norm_eq_abs), so |α v_I| ≤ ‖α‖.
3. For every I, t_I ≤ ‖α‖².
   - If StrictMono I: t_I = (α v_I)² = |α v_I|² (sq_abs) ≤ ‖α‖², by step 2 and 0 ≤ |α v_I| (pow_le_pow_left₀).
   - Otherwise: t_I = 0 ≤ ‖α‖² (positivity).
4. The type Fin n → Fin P has P^n elements (Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin). By Finset.sum_le_sum and step 3: Σ_I t_I ≤ Σ_I ‖α‖² = P^n·‖α‖² (Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ; simp [Finset.card_univ] closes this equality).
5. Real.sqrt is monotone (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt), so covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_I t_I) ≤ √(P^n·‖α‖²).
6. Since P^n ≥ 0, √(P^n·‖α‖²) = √(P^n)·√(‖α‖²) (Real.sqrt_mul). Since ‖α‖ ≥ 0, √(‖α‖²) = ‖α‖ (Real.sqrt_sq, norm_nonneg). With step 5: covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ √(P^n)·‖α‖.

No case distinction is needed:
- for n = 0 the index type has exactly one element and the empty product in step 1 is 1;
- for P = 0 < n the index type is empty and both sides are 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: unfold covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_I t_I) over I : Fin n → Fin P
basis vectors are unit vectors; ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm gives |α(b_{I(0)},…,b_{I(n−1)})| ≤ ‖α‖, hence t_I ≤ ‖α‖²
card(Fin n → Fin P) = P^n gives Σ_I t_I ≤ P^n·‖α‖²
Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, then √(P^n·‖α‖²) = √(P^n)·‖α‖ (Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq)

subproblems.title: Test forms have bounded Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P and every test form ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, there is C ∈ ℝ with C > 0 and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Here a test form is a ContDiff ℝ ∞ (smooth), compactly supported n-form x ↦ ω(x) ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n), ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Write ω also for the underlying form (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) : Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) n.

1. ω is smooth and has compact support.
   - The membership proof ω.property : ω ∈ TestFormOn U n = testFormOnSubmodule U n says IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ U.
   - Its first component IsTestForm ω is IsSmoothForm ω ∧ HasCompactSupport ω.
   - IsSmoothForm ω is by definition ContDiff ℝ ∞ ω, with ∞ the smoothness order in WithTop ℕ∞.
   Lean remark: in the contract scope, `open scoped ENNReal` makes a bare `∞` elaborate as the ℝ≥0∞ infinity. So keep this hypothesis as `IsSmoothForm ω` (from ω.property.1.1) and apply `ContDiff.continuous` to it; the definition unfolds by defeq.
2. A ContDiff map is continuous (ContDiff.continuous). A continuous map with compact support into a normed group is bounded (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous, the additive form of HasCompactMulSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). So there is B ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B for all x. In particular 0 ≤ ‖ω(0)‖ ≤ B (norm_nonneg).
3. Put D := √(P^n), so D ≥ 0 (Real.sqrt_nonneg), and C := D·B + 1. Since D ≥ 0 and B ≥ 0, C ≥ 1 > 0 (positivity).
4. Let x ∈ ℝ^P.
   - The sibling covector_norm (Submission.fiw_ims_sc_covectorNorm_le_opNorm P n (ω x)) gives covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ D·‖ω(x)‖.
   - Since D ≥ 0 and ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B: D·‖ω(x)‖ ≤ D·B (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left), and D·B ≤ D·B + 1 = C (linarith).
   - Hence covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ C for every x, and C > 0 by step 3. ∎
proof_key_steps: ω.property.1 : IsTestForm ω gives IsSmoothForm ω (ContDiff ℝ ∞) and HasCompactSupport ω
ContDiff.continuous and HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous: ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B for all x, with B ≥ 0
covector_norm: |ω(x)| ≤ √(P^n)·‖ω(x)‖ ≤ √(P^n)·B ≤ √(P^n)·B + 1 =: C > 0

subproblems.title: A null sequence of test forms is uniformly small in coefficient norm, with supports in one compact set
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and ω_q ∈ TestFormOn U n (q ∈ ℕ) with TestFormOnConverges ω 0. That is, there is a compact K₀ ⊆ U with tsupport ω_q ⊆ K₀ for all q and tsupport 0 ⊆ K₀, and for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_q → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0 uniformly on K₀ as q → ∞. Then there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_q ⊆ K for every q such that, for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large q, covectorEuclideanNorm(ω_q(x)) ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (ω : ℕ → TestFormOn U n), TestFormOnConverges ω 0 → ∃ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ U ∧ (∀ q, tsupport ((ω q : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n)) ⊆ K) ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ q in atTop, ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω q : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Write ω_q also for the underlying form (ω q : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n).

1. Unfold TestFormOnConverges ω 0 to obtain K with:
   - IsCompact K and K ⊆ U;
   - tsupport ω_q ⊆ K for every q (the inclusion for the zero form is not needed);
   - for every k ∈ ℕ, TendstoUniformlyOn (fun q x ↦ iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_q x) (fun x ↦ iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ↑(0 : TestFormOn U n) x) atTop K.
   Use this K. The first three conclusions hold, and only the last remains.
2. Let ε > 0. Put D := √(P^n) ≥ 0 (Real.sqrt_nonneg) and δ := ε/(D + 1) > 0 (positivity).
3. Take k = 0. By Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff applied with δ, for all sufficiently large q and every x ∈ K: dist(iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ↑(0 : TestFormOn U n) x, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_q x) < δ.
   - The coercion of the zero test form is the zero function, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 of the zero function is 0 at every point (simp; iteratedFDeriv_fun_zero). So the first argument is 0.
   - dist(0, y) = ‖y‖ (dist_zero_left), and ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f x‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero).
   - Hence ‖ω_q(x)‖ < δ for every x ∈ K.
4. Fix such a q and any x ∈ ℝ^P.
   - If x ∈ K, step 3 gives ‖ω_q(x)‖ ≤ δ.
   - If x ∉ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω_q, as tsupport ω_q ⊆ K. So ω_q(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and ‖ω_q(x)‖ = 0 ≤ δ.
   Hence ‖ω_q(x)‖ ≤ δ for every x.
5. The sibling covector_norm (Submission.fiw_ims_sc_covectorNorm_le_opNorm P n (ω_q x)) gives covectorEuclideanNorm(ω_q(x)) ≤ D·‖ω_q(x)‖.
   - By D ≥ 0 and step 4, this is ≤ D·δ = D·ε/(D + 1) (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left).
   - Finally D·ε/(D + 1) ≤ ε, because D·ε ≤ (D + 1)·ε for ε > 0 (div_le_iff₀ with D + 1 > 0; nlinarith).
6. Steps 3–5 show that for all sufficiently large q, covectorEuclideanNorm(ω_q(x)) ≤ ε for every x. That is, ∀ᶠ q in atTop, ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm(ω_q(x)) ≤ ε (filter_upwards). ∎
proof_key_steps: unpack TestFormOnConverges ω 0: a compact K ⊆ U containing all supports, plus uniform convergence of iteratedFDeriv ℝ k on K
k = 0 with Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff; iteratedFDeriv of the zero form is 0; dist_zero_left and norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero give eventually ‖ω_q(x)‖ < ε/(√(P^n)+1) on K
off K, ω_q(x) = 0 since tsupport ω_q ⊆ K (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport)
covector_norm: |ω_q(x)| ≤ √(P^n)·ε/(√(P^n)+1) ≤ ε for every x; filter_upwards

subproblems.title: A functional on test forms with local coefficient-sup-norm bounds is sequentially continuous at zero
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set and L : TestFormOn U n → ℝ any function. Assume that for every compact K ⊆ U there is A ∈ ℝ such that |L(ω)| ≤ A·C for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n and every C > 0 with tsupport ω ⊆ K and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ C for all x ∈ ℝ^P. Then for every sequence (ω_q) in TestFormOn U n with TestFormOnConverges ω 0, L(ω_q) → 0 as q → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (L : TestFormOn U n → ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ A : ℝ, ∀ (ω : TestFormOn U n) (C : ℝ), 0 < C → tsupport ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n)) ⊆ K → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C) → |L ω| ≤ A * C) → ∀ ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn U n, TestFormOnConverges ωs 0 → Tendsto (fun q => L (ωs q)) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Let (ω_q) = ωs satisfy TestFormOnConverges ωs 0. The sibling converges_small (Submission.fiw_ims_sc_converges_zero_small P n U ωs) gives a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_q ⊆ K for every q. Moreover, for every δ > 0 and all sufficiently large q, covectorEuclideanNorm(ω_q(x)) ≤ δ for every x.
2. Apply the hypothesis to this K (IsCompact K, K ⊆ U). It gives A ∈ ℝ with |L(ω)| ≤ A·C whenever C > 0, tsupport ω ⊆ K and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ C for all x.
3. By Metric.tendsto_nhds it suffices to show: for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large q, dist(L(ω_q), 0) < ε. Note dist(L(ω_q), 0) = |L(ω_q)| (Real.dist_eq, sub_zero). Let ε > 0 and put δ := ε/(|A| + 1) > 0 (positivity).
4. By step 1 with this δ, for all sufficiently large q, covectorEuclideanNorm(ω_q(x)) ≤ δ for every x.
   - For such q, apply step 2 with ω := ω_q and C := δ (δ > 0 and tsupport ω_q ⊆ K): |L(ω_q)| ≤ A·δ.
   - Since A ≤ |A| (le_abs_self) and δ ≥ 0, A·δ ≤ |A|·δ (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right).
5. |A|·δ = |A|·ε/(|A| + 1) < ε, because |A|·ε < (|A| + 1)·ε for ε > 0 (div_lt_iff₀ with |A| + 1 > 0; nlinarith with |A| ≥ 0).
   - Hence |L(ω_q)| < ε for all sufficiently large q (filter_upwards).
   - This proves Tendsto (fun q ↦ L(ω_q)) atTop (𝓝 0). Neither linearity of L nor a sign of A is used. ∎
proof_key_steps: converges_small gives a compact K ⊆ U containing all supports, with sup_x |ω_q(x)| → 0
the hypothesis on K gives A with |L ω| ≤ A·C for forms supported in K with |ω| ≤ C
for ε > 0 take δ = ε/(|A|+1): eventually |L(ω_q)| ≤ A·δ ≤ |A|·δ < ε
Metric.tendsto_nhds gives L(ω_q) → 0

subproblems.title: Integer-weighted series estimate in [0, ∞]: summability and |Σ c_r a_r| ≤ C·Σ|c_r| m_r
subproblems.statement: Let a : ℕ → ℝ, c : ℕ → ℤ, m : ℕ → [0, ∞] and C ∈ ℝ. Write |c_r| := ((c_r).natAbs : [0, ∞]). Assume ENNReal.ofReal|a_r| ≤ m_r·ENNReal.ofReal C for every r ∈ ℕ, and Σ'_r |c_r|·m_r < ∞ in [0, ∞]. Then r ↦ c_r·a_r (with c_r cast to ℝ) is summable in ℝ, and ENNReal.ofReal|Σ'_r c_r·a_r| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C·Σ'_r |c_r|·m_r.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℤ) (m : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞) (C : ℝ), (∀ r, ENNReal.ofReal |a r| ≤ m r * ENNReal.ofReal C) → (∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * m r) < ∞ → Summable (fun r => (c r : ℝ) * a r) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal |∑' r, (c r : ℝ) * a r| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C * ∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * m r
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: for r ∈ ℕ write |c_r| := ((c_r).natAbs : [0, ∞]) and x_r := (c_r : ℝ)·a_r. Let Σ := Σ'_r |c_r|·m_r ∈ [0, ∞]; Σ < ∞ by hypothesis. No sign condition on C is needed: if C ≤ 0 then ofReal C = 0, and the argument below covers that case unchanged.

1. For every r, ENNReal.ofReal|(c_r : ℝ)| = |c_r|.
   - |(c_r : ℝ)| is the real cast of the integer |c_r| (Int.cast_abs), which is the cast of the natural number (c_r).natAbs (Int.natCast_natAbs, Int.cast_natCast).
   - ENNReal.ofReal of the real cast of a natural number k equals (k : [0, ∞]) (ENNReal.ofReal_natCast).
2. Termwise bound. For every r:
   - ofReal|x_r| = ofReal(|(c_r : ℝ)|·|a_r|) (abs_mul);
   - = ofReal|(c_r : ℝ)|·ofReal|a_r| (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, since |(c_r : ℝ)| ≥ 0);
   - = |c_r|·ofReal|a_r| (step 1);
   - ≤ |c_r|·(m_r·ofReal C), multiplying the hypothesis ofReal|a_r| ≤ m_r·ofReal C on the left by |c_r|. Multiplication in [0, ∞] is monotone, so this holds also when c_r = 0 or m_r = ∞ (gcongr);
   - = ofReal C·(|c_r|·m_r) (commutativity and associativity; ring).
3. Sum step 2 over r (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum) and pull out the constant (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left): Σ'_r ofReal|x_r| ≤ Σ'_r ofReal C·(|c_r|·m_r) = ofReal C·Σ.
4. ofReal C < ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top) and Σ < ∞, so ofReal C·Σ < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top). With step 3, Σ'_r ofReal|x_r| ≠ ∞.
5. Summability.
   - By ENNReal.summable_toReal and step 4, r ↦ (ofReal|x_r|).toReal is summable in ℝ.
   - Since |x_r| ≥ 0, (ofReal|x_r|).toReal = |x_r| (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). So r ↦ |x_r| is summable.
   - Therefore r ↦ x_r = (c_r : ℝ)·a_r is summable (Summable.of_abs). This is the first conclusion.
6. On ℝ, ‖·‖ = |·| (Real.norm_eq_abs). By norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm, using the summability of r ↦ |x_r| from step 5, |Σ'_r x_r| ≤ Σ'_r |x_r|. Hence ofReal|Σ'_r x_r| ≤ ofReal(Σ'_r |x_r|) (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal).
7. Every |x_r| ≥ 0 and r ↦ |x_r| is summable (step 5), so ofReal(Σ'_r |x_r|) = Σ'_r ofReal|x_r| (ENNReal.ofReal_tsum_of_nonneg).
8. Chaining steps 6, 7 and 3: ofReal|Σ'_r (c_r : ℝ)·a_r| ≤ Σ'_r ofReal|x_r| ≤ ofReal C·Σ'_r |c_r|·m_r. This is the second conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: ofReal|(c_r : ℝ)| = ((c_r).natAbs : [0,∞]) (Int.cast_abs, Int.natCast_natAbs, ENNReal.ofReal_natCast)
termwise: ofReal|c_r a_r| ≤ ofReal C·(|c_r|·m_r) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, gcongr)
